title: Risk Calculation
cardSummary: An application that calculates insurance risk from a handful of inputs, built for the managers who help people get insured — not for actuaries.
sub: A web application that turns insurance risk assessment into a handful of inputs — built for the managers who help people get insured, not for actuaries.

cover.alt: Risk calculation dashboard on laptop and phone

sections.heading: Overview
sections.headline: Risk assessment in a handful of inputs
paragraphs: A web application for the managers who help people get insured, not for actuaries. It turns insurance risk assessment into a handful of inputs and shows the result so that it can be read at a glance.

sections.heading: 01 — Wireframes
sections.headline: From requirements to a first risk map
paragraphs: We collected the requirements and developed prototypes on top of them. Visual interactions and a UI kit followed.

sections.heading: 02 — Prototype
sections.headline: From a structural outline to realistic components
paragraphs: The prototype started as a structural outline. Once the client approved it, I moved to detailed prototypes built from realistic components — some elements were simplified, others rethought completely.

sections.heading: 03 — Visual design
sections.headline: Colour that carries meaning
paragraphs: Risk needed to be readable at a glance, so colour carries meaning throughout: you can tell which risk group something belongs to without reading a label.
A UI kit followed — colours, type, components and their states, documented for reuse.

result: Managers can now process a client's risk profile in under 2 minutes — down from around 10. That difference shows up directly in how many contracts they can close in a day.

designed.label: What I designed
designed.text: A web application that turns insurance risk assessment into a handful of inputs, with a risk-identification map and a documented UI kit.
